title: storage/AppSandbox
summary: AppSandbox.js — Per-app isolated, AES-256-GCM encrypted IndexedDB storage. Each app runs in its own IndexedDB database:  os.sandbox.<appId> completely separate from the kernel database (os.kernel). ── Isolation guarantees ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── • Different IDB database per app  → app A can never query app B's IDB. • Legacy records use AES-256-GCM with a key derived from a public OS fingerprint and app ID. That separates namespaces but does not provide secret-key confidentiality against someone who knows that fingerprint. • Enrolled private collections use openPagedStore(), backed by the kernel operator vault's random secret root, purpose keys and verified recovery. Collection migrations keep the legacy reader until copy verification and activation complete; the legacy key is never treated as a vault secret. ── API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const sb = new AppSandbox('os.calculator', cryptoDriver, { storage, operatorScope, operatorContext, }); await sb.init(); await sb.set('lastResult', 42);       // encrypt + store const v = await sb.get('lastResult'); // decrypt + return (null if missing) const keys = await sb.list();         // returns key names (not values) await sb.delete('lastResult'); await sb.clear();                     // wipe all of this app's data const info = sb.info();               // { appId, dbName, encrypted: true } ── Syscall surface (apps see syscalls.sandbox.*) ──────────────────────────── Created by createSandboxSyscalls(sandbox) exported below. Apps never receive a reference to AppSandbox directly.

name: createSandboxSyscalls
summary: Wrap an AppSandbox as the `syscalls.sandbox` namespace for an app. Apps receive this — they never get a reference to the AppSandbox itself. Usage in app code: await syscalls.sandbox.set('prefs', { theme: 'dark' }); const p = await syscalls.sandbox.get('prefs'); const keys = await syscalls.sandbox.list(); await syscalls.sandbox.delete('prefs'); await syscalls.sandbox.clear(); const { appId, dbName, encrypted } = syscalls.sandbox.info();

title: storage/LegacyOperatorMigration
summary: One-time ownership migration for data written before OperatorContext existed. A bounded subset of the pre-operator presentation state belonged to the only local user. Once there is exactly one verified Realm Passport and no rejected profile record, this service stages, verifies, and compare-and-swap promotes validated desktop shortcuts, Start pins, app settings, and window geometry into that Passport's operator namespace before account-owned subsystems bind. Authority-bearing state is intentionally excluded. Legacy sessions, grants, credentials, AppSandbox databases, and unsigned social state remain in their original quarantine and are never made authoritative by this migration. If an earlier V1 receipt exists, V3 inventories the account destination instead of trusting the retained source or the receipt's bounded summaries. It keeps only revalidated presentation files, moves every other exact-hash copy into internal quarantine, and blocks activation while any ambiguous file remains.

LegacyOperatorMigration may seed only strictly validated window geometry for one unambiguous Passport; every other historical localStorage record remains quarantined. AppSandbox publishes only newly attributable writes as authenticated account-and-device-bound ciphertext. OPFS fallback records and rebuildable caches are deliberately excluded because their authoritative data already lives elsewhere.

title: storage/SystemFS
summary: SystemFS.js — read-only virtual filesystem for the compiled-in OS. The engine, Plauna shell, editor, AGI runtime and the built-in apps are packaged directly into the OS bundle (ES modules compiled into the runtime). They are NOT stored in OPFS or IndexedDB, so they can never be edited, moved, or deleted — they are part of the system image. This driver surfaces them as a browsable, read-only tree mounted at `/system` so the Files app can SHOW where they live and clearly mark them immutable, while user/installed content (OPFS + IndexedDB) stays fully writable. Every entry returned carries `{ system: true, readOnly: true }` so the UI and the StorageManager guards can treat it as immutable. All methods are async to match the other storage drivers.

summary: system-docs.js — the "examples database" surfaced as the read-only /system tree. Goal: expose HOW to use each part of the compiled-in OS (engine, Plauna shell, editor, AGI runtime, built-in apps) WITHOUT shipping the proprietary source. Every leaf here is a usage/recipe document — it shows the public API and example calls a developer would write, not the implementation.
